svg.title: Typing "fat " at byte 4 of "the cat sat\n" in one array: every key moves every byte after it

g.title: The file is opened: its 12 bytes are read into a block exactly as big. The cursor is at byte 4, before "cat".
g.text: the file, read into one block

g.title: The first key, f, needs one byte more, and the block is full: the text moves to a block twice as big, 24 bytes, copying all 12 of them (grows 1). The 12 bytes of room are for the keys to come.
g.text: the block is full: a new one, twice as big

g.title: Key 1, f, at byte 4: the 8 bytes from 4 to the end move up one place to open a hole, and f goes into it: moved 8, 8 in all.
Key 2, a, at byte 5: the 8 bytes from 5 to the end move up one place to open a hole, and a goes into it: moved 8, 16 in all.
Key 3, t, at byte 6: the 8 bytes from 6 to the end move up one place to open a hole, and t goes into it: moved 8, 24 in all.
Key 4, a space, at byte 7: the 8 bytes from 7 to the end move up one place to open a hole, and a space goes into it: moved 8, 32 in all. Four keys, and each moved every byte after it.
goto 15, then "!": only the newline after the cursor moves up: moved 1. A key costs as many bytes as there are after it, wherever the text is kept in one array: 33 moved in all.
